proposal:
SCOPE. SKQ (sandwich kernel quotient) is an unimplemented root stage extending PSR. Everything here is hand-derived; nothing was run. It widens the detected family from symmetric formulas to symmetric core plus residue. It is not a completeness result and bounds no solver trace.

READING NEON-00021. Let a=x1+x2+x3, b=x4+x5+x6, c=x7+x8+x9, d=x10+x11+x12. Clauses 1-112 are six blocks encoding (-a or b), (-b or d), (-a or -d), (a or -c), (c or -d) and b!=c (two blocks on support 4..9 merge). Clauses 113-128 are one 8-variable block: a 16-point affine set with one point moved, so its stabilizer is trivial. Hence Sym(F)=0, matching the receipt's no_dimension_reduction. Clauses 1-112 alone are UNSAT. One rigid block switched compression off; the receipt does not show that this block made the trace harder.

MECHANISM. For any subspace K, not only Sym(F), let core_K(F) = {C in F : C^v in F for all v in K}, where C^v flips C's literals on supp(v). This is the largest K-invariant clause subset. Choose pivots P as in PSR and let G- be core_K(F) with x_P=0.
UNSAT side: G- UNSAT implies F UNSAT. The certificate is d*|core| syntactic lookups plus a pivot minor, with no 2^n enumeration.
SAT side: for block B and coset Q of K restricted to S_B, let f(B,Q)=|T_B meet Q|/|Q|. Let W*(K) be the sum over blocks of the largest f(B,Q) strictly between 0 and 1. If W*<1, every model of G- lifts to a model of F by conditional expectations over K. Otherwise a candidate lift is evaluated on F. If G- is SAT and no lift is found (the gap), SKQ skips and the original solver and order run unchanged.

DISCOVERY (bounded, incomplete). Compute A_B, the annihilator of Stab_B, per block. Keep all b blocks; repeatedly delete the block whose removal most increases n - rank(sum of kept A_B), ties to lower fill; record K at each strict increase. That is at most b^2 rank computations and at most n candidate kernels, each costing one coset-bucketing pass and one budgeted solve of a smaller formula. Soundness never depends on this search.

INDEPENDENT-TEST PREDICTIONS (not deployed-solver predictions).
R1, Neon-00021: peeling deletes the 8-variable block first. K={v : a(v)=b(v)=c(v)=d(v)=0}, dimension 8. Core = clauses 1-112 exactly. W*=16/256. With P={2,3,5,6,8,9,11,12}, G- = (-1,4),(-4,10),(-1,-10),(1,-7),(4,7),(7,-10),(-4,-7), which is UNSAT.
R2, 96-clause extra control: each added point sits alone in a 16-point coset, so W*=6/16 and F is equisatisfiable with the 6-clause quotient. This assumes the triple-XOR structure I infer from clause counts.
R3, 36-clause extra control: W*=9/4. Only the UNSAT side and witness evaluation apply; PSR's recode remains the tool.
R4, compression failure versus trace hardness: run the deployed solver on clauses 1-112 of Neon-00021 with the same order. A peak near 32 puts the cost in the lifted core, so the skip matters. A collapse means the rigid block drives the trace. I do not predict which. From the documented greedy ranking I expect v2 to skip that sub-formula as an incompatible basis, because the merged block's space is span{b+c} while greedy picks b and c; that reading is unverified.

FAILURE MODE. Deleting one clause per block, instead of adding one, makes every coset partial: the core is empty and SKQ returns nothing. That is the perturbed-XOR regime of auto00009.
missing_theorem:
T3 (elementary, unformalised; a conjecture until machine-checked). Let F be duplicate-free and tautology-free, K a subspace of dimension d, P pivots onto which K projects bijectively. (a) core_K(F) is the largest K-invariant sub-CNF. (b) G- UNSAT implies F UNSAT. (c) If W*(K)<1, each model y of G- has at least (1-W*)*2^d lifts satisfying F, so #F >= (1-W*)*2^d*#G-, and conditional expectations find one using rank computations only. Idea for (c): for uniform k in K, (y,0)+k restricted to S_B is uniform on one coset; a full coset is impossible because the core is K-invariant and y satisfies G-; a union bound over blocks finishes. First step: state (b) and (c) in Lean beside CompressionSoundness and kernel-check R1. The complete-enumeration rule does not cover this certificate.

T4 (first genuinely missing; open). MAX-KERNEL: given a width-w block CNF and d, is there K with dim K >= d and W*(K)<1? I conjecture NP-hardness for some constant w. It contains a minimum-distance-type problem (a nonzero v violating the fewest stabilizer constraints). Vardy's theorem covers general codes; I have not checked bounded width, and two-variable forms reduce to min-cut. If hard, peeling's honest scope is 't rigid blocks at cost b^(t+1)'. If easy, K becomes canonical.

T2 (carried, open). Nothing links G- to the deployed trace; peak(G-) <= peak(F) is unproved even in the exact case.

GAP (open). When G- is SAT and W*>=1 there is no work bound.
self_attack:
1. This is still family detection: symmetric core plus low-fill residue. The gap is as hard as general SAT: for F = G(forms) and H(pivot variables) with H arbitrary, the core is the lifted G and deciding F still requires solving H. No universality follows.
2. Peeling is greedy and plateaus whenever two rigid blocks must be removed together. Nothing shows it finds a good K when one exists.
3. The core is fragile in the other direction. One missing clause drops its whole coset, so perturbed nonlinear gadgets can leave an empty core. Completing cosets instead gives a stronger formula, useful only for finding witnesses.
4. W*<1 is a union bound and fails with many defect blocks; R3 already fails at nine. A local-lemma version would need independence over linear forms, which I have not worked out.
5. Up to n extra budgeted solves are added, none with a polynomial bound. When every candidate lands in the gap, SKQ is pure overhead.
6. A smaller G- need not have a smaller peak. The R3 control already peaks 0 on the deployed solver, so SKQ may repair compression where no trace problem existed. R4 tests exactly that on Neon-00021.
7. R1 was checked by hand only. R2 and R3 assume structure inferred from clause counts. The v2 skip reason in R4 assumes my reading of the greedy ranking.
8. Not new mathematics: relaxed or 'almost' symmetries appear in the symmetry-breaking literature (from memory, uncited). The contribution is the linear-algebra form and the certificate split.
9. The watcher handoff contributed nothing usable.
mechanism_signature: SKQ | root, unimplemented | K = any subspace, not only Sym(F) | core_K(F) = clauses whose whole K-orbit lies in F (a clause subset) | G- = core at pivots 0, subclauses only | UNSAT: G- UNSAT => F UNSAT; certificate = d*|core| syntactic lookups + pivot minor | SAT: slack W* = sum over blocks of max partial-coset fill; W*<1 => lift by conditional expectations; else evaluate witness on F | discovery: greedy block peeling, <= b^2 rank computations, <= n kernels | gap (G- SAT, no lift) => skip, solver and order unchanged | diagnostics (d, |core|, W*, gap flag)
delta_from_prior: PSR (00024) required F^v = F exactly, so one rigid block reduced K to zero; Neon-00021 is that case. SKQ quotients by the kernel of a sub-formula and makes the residue canonical through core_K. FSL (00023) summed every residue clause in its union bound; W* sums one coset per block, which is never larger. New this round: the core operator, the UNSAT/SAT certificate split, per-coset slack, peeling with a stated cost bound, the hand analysis of Neon-00021 (R1), the trace-separating test R4, and the MAX-KERNEL question. Kept: pivot restriction, T1, T2. Not superseded: PSR's bijective recode, still the only proposal for the sigma = 9/4 control.
